extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX coordinators, higher-education officials, legal counsel, advocates, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements for recipients' responses, grievance processes, definitions, and enforcement under the Department of Education's final Title IX sexual harassment regulations, as explained in the preamble/response-to-comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and supportive response to complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must respond promptly to complainants in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent, including offering supportive measures irrespective of whether a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a) revised to state recipients must offer supportive measures to each complainant, and the Title IX Coordinator must contact the complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint. The Department emphasizes sensitivity to trauma and that contacting and offering supports is an affirmative obligation on recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process fair to both parties (§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed grievance process gives complainants and respondents equally strong, clear procedural rights during a grievance process and is intended to be fair to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process reflects the seriousness of sexual harassment and the life-altering consequences of determinations; it is rooted in due process principles, aims for factually accurate and reliable determinations, and prescribes consistent procedures for investigation and adjudication when a formal complaint is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and avoidance of bias or conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX personnel and recipients must maintain impartiality, avoid bias and conflicts of interest, and not automatically believe or disbelieve either complainants or respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations impose duties on recipients and their Title IX personnel to maintain impartiality, avoid bias and conflicts, and ensure objective evaluation of evidence relevant to each situation so determinations are impartial and reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and remedies for findings of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When a respondent is found responsible following a grievance process that complies with §106.45, recipients must effectively implement remedies designed to restore or preserve a complainant's equal educational access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not require particular disciplinary sanctions but requires remedies for complainants. The obligation to provide remedies follows a compliant grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-deliberate indifference standard for recipients' responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's response must not be 'clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances' — i.e., not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard, combined with particular requirements for a prompt response that includes offering supportive measures, balances requiring meaningful responses while permitting discretion to address unique needs of each complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded definition of sexual harassment (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'sexual harassment' is revised to expressly include domestic violence, dating violence, and stalking as those offenses are defined under VAWA (amending the Clery Act), as well as sexual assault and quid pro quo harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change clarifies that Title IX covers these forms of misconduct and signals that recipients must respond when such conduct falls within Title IX's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of application across demographic characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations define the scope of Title IX and recipients' legal obligations without regard to race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, or other characteristics of a person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states the regulations protect all individuals and apply irrespective of demographic characteristics, stressing intersectional concerns were considered though the rules apply universally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of evidence and reliable determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations must be investigated and adjudicated impartially, without bias, and based on objective evaluation of the evidence relevant to each situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether false accusations are frequent or rare, the §106.45 grievance process requires impartial investigation and adjudication to reach reliable determinations and to ensure appropriate remedies when responsibility is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to an advisor (advisor need not be an attorney)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party has the right to choose an advisor to assist the party; the advisor is not required to be an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(5)(iv) expressly gives each party the right to choose an advisor, addressing concerns about burdens to marginalized individuals to pay for representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not excuse or ignore sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not permitted under the final regulations to excuse or ignore sexual harassment, nor to avoid investigating where a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a) obligates recipients to respond by offering supportive measures to complainants; §106.45 obligates recipients to conduct investigations and provide remedies when respondents are found responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to adopt alternate investigation/adjudication models and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and States remain free to consider alternate investigation and adjudication models, including regional centers and independent investigatory/adjudicatory bodies, and to adopt best practices for supporting survivors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will offer technical assistance for pursuing regional center models; recipients can form voluntary cooperative organizations or rely on State-operated independent investigators/adjudicators while still meeting obligations under the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department enforcement and legally enforceable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations create legally enforceable requirements for when and how recipients must respond, and the Department will vigorously enforce Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects claims the rules were designed to protect institutions' financial interests and emphasizes administrative enforcement as its focus; the rules may also have the ancillary benefit of decreasing litigation by prescribing administrative grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may provide prevention, education, and counseling (not mandated)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the final regulations focus on required responses, recipients are not precluded from offering counseling, mental health services, prevention education (e.g., consent training, bystander intervention), or other measures to prevent sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not mandate educational curricula but acknowledges prevention efforts remain within the purview of schools, experts, and advocates and that the regulations do not impede such activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' obligations extend to employee and administrator misconduct notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If a school employee (including administrators) engages in conduct on the basis of sex described in §106.30, the recipient must respond promptly whenever the school has notice of the conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition of Title IX sexual harassment includes quid pro quo harassment by any recipient's employee and sexual assault by any individual; recipient obligations to respond apply regardless of perpetrator's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with constitutional rights (§106.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations requires a recipient to restrict rights guaranteed under the U.S. Constitution, including rights to equal protection and substantive due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes §106.6(d) explicitly addresses intersections with constitutional safeguards and that final regulations were crafted with those considerations in mind.
